top3.headline: Thoughtworks Trials Pocock skills, Caution on skill libraries
top3.whyItMatters: Adopt skills one by one; whole libraries can outrun your team's judgment.

top3.headline: Terminal-Bench repairs lift accuracy over 10 points
top3.whyItMatters: Broken tasks quietly skew agent scores, so treat leaderboards as provisional.

top3.headline: Opus 5.5 fails twice as often on max as on high
top3.whyItMatters: Defaulting to max reasoning can cut reliability; prefer high until the gap is explained.

items.title: Karpathy one-shots TristanTube, 47K videos, in three minutes
items.takeaway: Karpathy turned Tristan Hume's YouTube tier list into TristanTube with 47K videos and TV mode, one-shotted with Claude Code in 3 minutes.
items.soWhat: Personal media apps are becoming weekend one-shots for people who already ship with agents.

items.title: Meng To has Opus recreate his room in three.js
items.takeaway: Meng To asked Opus 5.5 to recreate his room in three.js so it can animate his tutorial videos, combining 3D and motion design.
items.soWhat: Creators are using coding agents as production 3D tools, not just demos.

items.title: Approved China H200 firm New Matrix shows an empty office
items.takeaway: The Verge, citing NYT: New Matrix, approved for Nvidia H200 chips, lists an empty office and owners tied to a PE firm blacklisted since 2024.
items.soWhat: Export approvals for AI chips may outrun vetting of who actually receives them.

items.title: Replit CEO: $10M software projects shrink to $250K on Replit
items.takeaway: In a YC interview with Paul Graham, Amjad Masad says banks and manufacturers replace $10M software projects with $250K of Replit; the figure is his claim, not audited.
items.soWhat: Enterprise software budgets are the next battleground if agent platforms keep that promise.

items.title: Thoughtworks puts Pocock skills in Trial, warns on skill libraries
items.takeaway: November Radar puts mattpocock/skills in Trial, Caution on skill cognitive surrender, and Adopt for agent sandboxing; Linear, OpenSpec, and Git AI move to Trial.
items.soWhat: Evaluate each agent skill on its own; do not adopt whole skill libraries blindly.

items.title: Claude CFO prompt audits bank CSVs without account access
items.takeaway: Ruben Hassid exports 12 months of bank CSVs, opens the folder in Claude Opus 5.5 High, and runs a be-my-CFO prompt; he reports a Stripe fee cut worth $10,200 a year.
items.soWhat: You can get finance-agent value from local CSVs without handing over bank logins.

items.title: Macs quietly build an on-device personal knowledge graph
items.takeaway: Researchers document macOS daemons building a plaintext on-device graph of you and contacts; they open-sourced iKnow to inspect it. HN: 413 points, 238 comments.
items.soWhat: Leaders on Macs should assume a rich personal graph already exists on disk.

items.title: Opus 5.5 fails twice as often on max reasoning as on high
items.takeaway: T3 Code telemetry via Adam Holter: Opus 5.5 fails twice as many turns on max as on high in every turn-length bucket; most extra failures hit in the first 30 seconds.
items.soWhat: Treat max reasoning as a risk setting until vendors explain the failure spike.

items.title: Terminal-Bench 2.1 fixes show 30% of tasks had issues
items.takeaway: arXiv 2611.08417 audited Terminal-Bench 2.0, found issues in ~30% of tasks, released 2.1; repairs raised accuracy over 10 points and moved ranks by up to three.
items.soWhat: Budget continuous validation if you buy or sell agent performance claims.
